notes: Perfect claim overlap (C87, C88, C107, C108, C115) regarding conformational changes during transport. LLM finds evidence well-supported that AMTs undergo conformational changes contradicting rigid channel model. Peer reviewers challenge this interpretation, stating it conflates binding with transport and that binding-induced changes without major conformational shifts could explain the data.

Both address mechanistic ambiguity (C90, C100) regarding whether fluorescence reports binding vs. transport. LLM rates UNCERTAIN acknowledging data cannot distinguish mechanisms. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the authors' acknowledgment of this uncertainty, though they want it discussed more thoroughly throughout the paper. Both agree the ambiguity exists.

Partial overlap (C89 shared, plus C72 from LLM). LLM finds the correlation between transport activity and fluorescence well-supported through multiple validation lines including mutant studies. Peer reviewers are uncertain, stating they are 'not at all convinced that the signal reports transport activity' and believe authors conflate transport with substrate binding.

Strong overlap (C7, C49, C54, C57 shared). Both agree the technical development of AmTrac by cpGFP insertion with systematic optimization is well-documented and convincing. Peer reviewers explicitly state work is 'convincing, satisfying, and carefully done'.

Partial overlap (C59, C60, C61 shared). Both agree on the electrophysiological characterization showing similar Km values and that fluorescence correlates with concentration-dependent responses. Peer reviewers affirm the signal 'nicely tracks the NH4+ transport activity as measured directly by voltage-clamp methods'.

Good overlap (C65, C66, C67, C68 shared). Both agree on sensor reversibility, concentration-dependence, and selectivity data. Peer reviewers accept the Km measurements and selectivity findings without raising concerns about these specific technical characterizations.

Partial overlap (C52, C76 shared). Both agree on the generalizability and value of the approach. LLM emphasizes successful sensor creation for AMT1;2 and MEP2. Peer reviewers affirm 'these reporters represent an important technical advance' and may be 'quite valuable' for studying ammonium handling.

Partial overlap (C10, C11 shared). Both agree the technology represents an important advance for monitoring transporter activity. LLM emphasizes in vivo monitoring capabilities; peer reviewers affirm the 'important technical advance' and potential value for research applications.

Minimal overlap (C72 shared). LLM finds mutant data strongly support that fluorescence reports transport-related processes. Peer reviewers are uncertain, stating 'Perhaps the suppressor screen experiments argue for actual transport, but this would require more information on binding and how this might be differentiated in the mutants'.

Minimal overlap (C74 shared). LLM finds AmTrac-100μ development with altered kinetics well-supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether mutant data definitively distinguish transport from binding, requiring more information to interpret the findings.

Minimal overlap (C111 shared). Both agree the work represents a conceptual advance. LLM emphasizes monitoring activity states vs. just conformational changes. Peer reviewers affirm the technical advance and value of the approach, though they question some mechanistic interpretations elsewhere.

Minimal overlap (C8, C58 shared). Both agree on concentration-dependent fluorescence response being well-demonstrated. This represents the basic technical observation that reviewers accept, separate from mechanistic interpretation disputes.
Claims C70, C71 about linker optimization and improved variants only evaluated by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found. LLM finds systematic screening of ~350 variants well-documented.

Claims C86, C116, C117, C119, C120, C121 about future applications and required follow-up only evaluated by LLM. These speculative statements about future directions are appropriately rated UNCERTAIN by LLM as untested hypotheses.

Large set of background claims (C1-C48) about ammonium biology, transporter function, and methodological context only explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers. These established knowledge claims provide accepted context and are not questioned.
